exposure: mode of birth (cesarean delivery vs. vaginal with forceps/vacuum)
cohort: The study included 202 women who self-identified as having experienced a traumatic childbirth.
finding: Perceived stress levels and duration showed a significant positive association with post-traumatic stress disorder symptoms, with longer stress being linked to greater severity.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was linked to higher post-traumatic stress disorder scores compared to vaginal delivery with forceps or vacuum extraction, mediated by increased perceived stress.
